goal: Build a local-first, content-addressed, versioned, searchable, replayable Project Corpus that preserves success, failure, partial, and repair history without becoming a second Knowledge or runtime authority.
acceptance_criteria: all project outcomes, including failed and aborted attempts, can be captured
source snapshots reconstruct with byte fidelity and content-hash integrity
private evaluator packets, secrets, machine paths, and quarantined material never enter normal search or benchmark packets
family-level split governance prevents sibling and near-duplicate leakage
a real FAIL to REPAIR to PASS chain is fully recoverable
full repository regression finishes with zero failures and zero errors before release

quality_metrics.method: reconstruction, verification, and catalog rebuild tests

quality_metrics.measure: secret, private evaluator, and absolute-path leakage

quality_metrics.method: deterministic family split and leakage checker

quality_metrics.target: 0 false COMPLETE entries and project outcome unaffected
quality_metrics.method: fault injection and best-effort hook tests
required gates, domain suites, and full pytest

improvement: use captured failure chains to prepare future complexity benchmarks without training or changing generation behavior

interface_expectations: CapabilityTree, ExecutionDAG, FileRunStore, and ProjectBlueprint remain canonical authorities
Corpus capture is an application-level best-effort observer and cannot change project outcomes
real corpus content remains external and local; Git contains only code, schemas, docs, and sanitized examples
